(d)->D, with no question numbering its options any other way. DECIMALS ARE ORDINARY IN THE PAPER: the paper's only decimal, Q8 option (b), prints 'x = 1.5' with a baseline full stop, while the marking scheme prints the same value raised as '1·5' — the paper wins (see the Q8 _flag). Headings are 'Case Study-I / -II / -III' (Roman numerals, hyphen with no spaces), kept out of context and recorded in _caseStudyLabel; sub-parts are labelled (I)/(II)/(III). SECTION E OF THIS SET IS IDENTICAL TO 65/5/1's — same three passages, same sub-parts, and even the same case-study NUMBERS, so no re-labelling was needed. All 20 Section-A keys come from the official marking scheme for THIS code (ms/p02.png-p06.png, 'MS_XII_Mathematics_041_65/5/3_2022-23'); every one of the 14 reused MCQs independently matched the key the reference file already carried. Unlike 65/5/1 this set has NO keyless question. 33 of the 52 rows are questions 65/5/1 also sets: each was read on the 65/5/3 page first, then its stem and options reused byte-for-byte from data/2023-65-5-1.questions.json so the rows dedup at commit instead of shipping a one-character drift. plan.txt's block->number attribution proved unreliable as the brief warns (e.g. it maps this paper's Q22 to 65/5/1's Q21, which is a completely different question), so every match was made on CONTENT. NO solutions written for subjective rows, per the brief.

questions.context:
An equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to the independent variables is called a differential equation. A differential equation of the form \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F(x, y)\) is said to be homogeneous if F(x, y) is a homogeneous function of degree zero, whereas a function F(x, y) is a homogenous function of degree n if \(F(\lambda x, \lambda y) = \lambda^n F(x, y)\). To solve a homogeneous differential equation of the type \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F(x, y) = g\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\), we make the substitution \(y = vx\) and then separate the variables.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Show that \((x^2 - y^2)\,dx + 2xy\,dy = 0\) is a differential equation of the type \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\).
